ideas.pitch: A compact computer vision module using a webcam and microcontroller to sort recyclable waste in real-time, built specifically for Crescent Institute campus waste bins.
ideas.title: CobotVision: Edge AI Garbage Classifier for Campus Sustenance
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the winning pattern of practical robotics and computer vision builds like ROBOTICS-ai-garbage-classifier, targeting a tangible campus utility that judges can test immediately.

ideas.pitch: A low-cost IoT accelerometer and GPS hardware prototype attached to campus buggies or two-wheelers that automatically dispatches emergency coordinates upon impact detection.
ideas.title: AutoSOS-Crescent: ESP32 Post-Accident Campus Vehicle Alert
ideas.why_it_could_win: Replicates the winning formula of physical IoT hardware and accident detection seen in Auto-SOS-Smart-post-accident-detection-and-response-system, standing out instantly against software-only web apps in an in-person room.

ideas.pitch: A miniature differential-drive rover utilizing camera line-following and obstacle avoidance to transport small documents between department offices on campus.
ideas.title: CrescentFleet: Autonomous Indoor Delivery Rover Prototype
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the physical robotics execution style of International Hackathon winners, giving judges a physical machine to watch move around the presentation desk.

ideas.pitch: A secure IoT lab equipment locker system with an ESP8266 microcontroller, physical solenoid lock, and a real-time web dashboard tracking student check-outs.
ideas.title: SmartLock-Crescent: RFID and App-Based Lab Asset Tracker
ideas.why_it_could_win: Adopted from BoilerMake XII winning smart lock systems, providing a utilitarian physical demo that solves a real college-level resource management problem.

ideas.pitch: An edge-computing sensor node monitoring lab temperature, humidity, and power draw, running a lightweight isolation forest algorithm to flag anomalies before equipment fails.
ideas.title: LabGuard-AI: IoT Energy and Environment Anomaly Detector
ideas.why_it_could_win: Translates the multi-agent IoT diagnostic logic from SEAL Hackathon winners into a streamlined, low-overhead hardware anomaly detector built for 24-hour feasibility.
